translation.english_title: He who labours for the village, di

english_lines: He who labours for the village, di,
Knows not a single wrong, di,
Gets kicked and dies, di — buffalo calf.
notes: The colloquial vocative force carried by the joined source forms ending in `டி` is retained as `di` rather than formalized away.
`எருமைக் கன்னுக்குட்டி` remains the concrete buffalo-calf refrain/image.

english_lines: There is no time for what is good,
Everything that happens is outward show,
Say it plainly — it is a shame — buffalo calf.
notes: The social accusation is kept direct; `வெளிப்பகட்டு` is rendered as outward show rather than softened to mere appearance.

english_lines: The fellow who lives by cheating,
But the man who contradicts his word,
notes: The palace-versus-begging contrast and the spoken/rustic attack are preserved instead of recast as neutral social commentary.
`எகத்தாளம் போடுறானே` is rendered with its performative swagger rather than reduced to `lives proudly`.

english_lines: He talks till we believe him to be the leader of the land,
Then scoops away all the wealth he wants, di;
With the land's prosperity in mind, the poor man labours all day,
For the poor, no good times; all sorts of fellows are thriving —
notes: The verified Tamil witness prints the joined form `வேணசெல்வம்`; the English renders its contextual force as `all the wealth he wants` without asserting a Tamil emendation.
The verified source also prints `பெண்ணி`. The English follows the sentence's evident prosperity/labour contrast while leaving that Tamil witness unchanged and explicitly documented.
The leader/wealth/poor-worker sequence is kept as a pointed political-social satire rather than generalized.

translator_notes: The source context label `மாட்டுக்காரப் பையன்` is understood as a cattle-boy/cowherd performance voice but is not used to invent a named character.
The translation retains `di` selectively because removing the repeated colloquial address would erase part of the song's rustic spoken force.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
